sentences.text: Now we descend to the surface: before you is Curiosity.
This car-sized robot, weighing 1 ton, landed in Gale Crater in August 2012, lowered on cables by a sky crane.
It generates its energy from the heat of plutonium, so it is unaffected by dust storms.
It proved that a lake lasting millions of years once existed on the crater floor, and it found the chemical ingredients needed for life.
For more than 10 years it has been climbing the slopes of Mount Sharp, reading Mars's climate history layer by layer.
Deimos is Mars's smaller and more distant moon.
Its diameter is about 12 kilometers, and it circles the planet in 30 hours.
Its surface is smoother than Phobos's, because its craters are filled with a thick layer of dust.
Seen from the surface of Mars, it is no different from a bright star.
It is still debated whether both moons are captured asteroids or the remnants of a giant collision; Japan's MMX mission will bring a sample from Phobos to answer this question.
Before we leave Mars, let's look back once more.
Today nearly a dozen active vehicles are operating in its orbit and on its surface.
The findings are consistent: Mars was once a warm, moist, and perhaps habitable world.
When it lost its magnetic field, the solar wind swept its atmosphere into space, and the planet turned into a cold desert.
Even so, the first planet humanity will one day set foot on will most likely be this one.
Our Mars tour has come to an end.
Welcome to the Mars tour.
The Red Planet is the fourth planet from the Sun, and the world humanity has sent the most vehicles to.
Its day is very similar to Earth's: 24 hours and 37 minutes.
Its year, though, is 687 days.
Its atmosphere is very thin and consists almost entirely of carbon dioxide; the average temperature is minus 60 degrees.
Even so, there is ice at its poles, and dried-up riverbeds and ancient lake beds on its surface.
And Perseverance, the most advanced robot on Mars.
It landed in Jezero Crater in February 2021; this is an ancient delta where a river emptied into a lake 3. 5 billion years ago.
Its mission is to search for traces of past microbial life and to fill titanium tubes with rock samples, leaving them for a future mission to bring to Earth.
The small helicopter it brought with it, Ingenuity, became the first vehicle to fly on another planet, and it carried out 72 flights instead of the planned 5.
The MOXIE experiment, for its part, opened the way for future astronauts by producing oxygen from the air of Mars.
The larger of Mars's two small moons is Phobos.
It is a potato-shaped rock only 22 kilometers wide.
It orbits at a distance of 6,000 kilometers from the planet; this is the closest orbit of any moon in the Solar System.
It is so fast that it circles Mars in 7 hours and 39 minutes, and seen from the surface of Mars it rises in the west.
It is dropping by 2 meters every century; within about 50 million years it will either crash into Mars or break apart and turn into a ring.
